summary: Bare Point Light at Chemainus Bay, Vancouver Island: lit 1897 for the lumber trade, kept by resident keepers until 1926, now a cylindrical tower beside an oil terminal.

structures.note: Wooden dwelling with a square lantern on its roof (1897 description). LighthouseFriends says it was burned in 1940; Rowlett says it was demolished about 1940.
White cylindrical tower with a green band at the top (CCG). Dated around 1980 by LighthouseFriends and Rowlett. Material not stated in the sources read.

access.note: The point is occupied by a Shell Canada oil terminal. No public access is described in the sources read. LighthouseFriends advises viewing the light from a boat.

events.note: Station established; first keeper hired 12 June 1897
James Crozier appointed at $120 a year
Floating landing built at the point (fiscal year ended 30 June 1900), $36
Gale swept away the floating landing (March 1911)
Keeper's wife found drowned after 4 August 1912; the keeper did not return to the light
Keeper James Chalmers found dead on the floor of the light in September 1926
Light left unwatched; an unwatched AGA acetylene light placed in the lantern
LighthouseFriends: the dilapidated lighthouse was burned. Rowlett gives demolished about 1940.
Steel skeletal tower with a red lantern placed on the point (LighthouseFriends)
White circular (cylindrical) tower replaced the skeletal tower, around 1980

keepers.name: James Crozier
keepers.note: Appointed 12 June 1897 at $120 a year. Also a lumber inspector at the Chemainus sawmill with the Marine Agent's permission (LighthouseFriends). LighthouseFriends says he resigned in 1911.

keepers.name: Philip R. Stevenson
keepers.note: Printed as P. R. Stevinson on the Bare Point line of the 1913 keeper list (scan 81, printed p. 74; checked on the page image), where the same row gives appointment 14 October 1910. LighthouseFriends dates his taking charge to 1911, after Crozier resigned. Stroke in April 1912 (LighthouseFriends). Never returned to the light after August 1912.

keepers.name: James Chalmers
keepers.note: Printed as J. C, Chalmers on the Bare point line of the 1915 keeper list (scan 77, printed p. 70; checked on the page image), appointed 5 August 1912. LighthouseFriends gives James Chalmers; the initials J. C. are not reconciled. Found dead at his post in September 1926.

keepers.name: Charles Laurence
keepers.note: Named only in a 2018 Chemainus Courier column reprinted by the Chemainus Valley Museum, which says he rowed across the harbour daily to light the lantern. No date and no Department record read for this story.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record notes that OpenStreetMap shows a structure standing while LighthouseFriends says it is lost. The 1897 wooden dwelling is gone (burned or demolished about 1940, the sources disagree). The cylindrical tower standing today dates from about 1980 and appears in the Canadian Coast Guard list.

LighthouseFriends and Rowlett both describe the 1940 change at the point. The two accounts differ on how the 1897 house ended (burned in LighthouseFriends, demolished in Rowlett) and are kept as a disagreement in the story.

The 1913 keeper list gives P. R. Stevinson's appointment on the Bare point row as 14 October 1910; LighthouseFriends dates Stevenson's taking charge to 1911, after Crozier resigned. The story states both; the roster uses the Department date.

notes_for_editor: Thin-to-moderate evidence. Primary Department of Marine material in the local corpus: the 1900 keeper statement (p. 133, Crozier, 12 June 1897, $120) and the 1900 floating-landing line (p. 62). The 1913 and 1915 keeper lists were checked on the page images: the Bare point row carries P. R. Stevinson (appointed 14 October 1910) in 1913 and J. C. Chalmers (appointed 5 August 1912) in 1915. The 1900 statement line carries Crozier's name on the Bare Point row (scan 230, printed p. 133), checked on the image. The 1897 description of the light is taken from LighthouseFriends quoting the 1897 report; the 1897 volume is not in the local corpus (it starts in 1900). The March 1911 gale, the August 1912 drowning, the September 1926 death and the 1940 fate of the house rest on LighthouseFriends alone; no Marine report in the corpus names them (the corpus ends in 1924), and the Victoria Daily Colonist, which would cover the 1912 and 1926 deaths, was not reachable. LighthouseFriends and Rowlett disagree on the 1940 fate (burned vs demolished), which the story states. Keeper James Chalmers: the Department prints J. C. Chalmers; LighthouseFriends gives James; not reconciled. Charles Laurence appears only in a 2018 newspaper column reprinted by the Chemainus Valley Museum; no Department list read names him. Same-name trap: the 1924 Marine report mentions a 'Bare point breakwater' with an Aga light, which is Port Arthur, Ontario, and is not used. The story has six chapter headings although the moderate-length rule suggests two to four; the chapters are kept because each holds a sourced paragraph, and they can be merged if the editor prefers. Record check: the coordinates and characteristic (Fl G 4s, 9.3 m, 5 nm) match the CCG list; no correction proposed. ARLHS page was not reachable (certificate error).
